params.place: on the map: West Africa, Gambia inside Senegal

moments.what: the thin river country fills red, a little boat already sailing up it
Senegal fills green all around it
the red strip wriggles like a worm
the camera settles on the river mouth where the sea bites in

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Why does Gambia sit inside Senegal, like a worm inside an apple?

params.place: on the map: Banjul at the river mouth, then all of Senegal

moments.what: the camera pushes in on Banjul, a girl reaches up
she plants the Gambian flag on the map
a seller on the riverbank fans out banknotes
the camera pulls back, Senegal fills green and arrows curl round the strip
the coast lights up, the one open side

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Gambia is a real country, with its own flag and its own money, and Senegal wraps around it on every side but the sea.

params.place: on the map: the whole strip from the coast

moments.what: a surveyor walks a long measuring tape up the river
the tape reaches the far end, its tag shows the length
the camera drops close to a short crosswise tape
the short tape snaps tight, its tag shows the width

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: From the coast, it runs almost 480 km inland, yet at its widest it is only about 50 km across.

params.place: on the map: a crossing on the border

moments.what: the guard lifts the barrier
a minibus crosses
the border starts drawing itself
the camera pulls back as the line runs round the strip, the length lands on a tag
huts pop up along the border
baobabs pop up

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Senegal is its only neighbour, and their border winds on for 749 km, through villages, farms and forest.

params.place: on the map: the river mouth at Banjul

moments.what: a gull crosses the map
the river lights up
a tall ship sails in from the ocean
peanut boats travel upriver, the camera follows them inland
the camera swings back, a fort and the British flag land at the mouth
a soldier points out to sea

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: So how did that happen? The answer is the river. In the age of sailing ships, it was a highway deep into Africa, and Britain held its mouth.

params.place: on the map: the land north and south of the river

moments.what: a French officer plants the tricolour north of the river
flags pop up all over the land
the camera pulls back: flags ring the river
the land fills green
the name stamps across it

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: France held the land all around it, the colony that became Senegal.

params.place: on the old treaty map: the river's middle

moments.what: the map turns old, the year lands at its head
a British and a French diplomat walk towards each other on the map
they shake hands
a pen traces the river in red
ruled lines are drawn either side
the gap is measured, the camera closes in

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: So in 1889, the two empires made a deal. Britain kept the river, and land about 10 km back from its banks.

params.place: on the map: Banjul and the whole strip

moments.what: French flags drop onto the land around the strip
the land fills green
the camera dives to Banjul, a crowd raises the Gambian flag
the year lands on a banner over the city
the camera pulls back, the border lights up
it pulses, unchanged

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: France took everything else. In 1965, Gambia became independent, inside exactly the same line.

params.place: on the map: both countries from above

moments.what: the camera pushes in
both flags are planted
the two countries flood one colour, the first year lands
the joined name lands across them
the border cracks white, the map shakes, the colours snap back
the tag flips to the second year

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: So did anyone ever fix it? In 1982, the two countries even joined as one, Senegambia. By 1989, they had split again.

params.place: on the map at dusk: the river close, then the country from above

moments.what: a fisherman's boat glides past a white border stone
more boats drift by in the evening light
the camera lifts high above the river
Gambia lights up red, a thin strip along the water
the border traces itself all the way round

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: So a line drawn for river boats, about 10 km from the water, is still where a whole country begins and ends.

params.place: Africa from space, then back down to West Africa

moments.what: Gambia glows red in the west
Lesotho glows red inside South Africa
a question mark bounces between the two
the camera swoops back towards West Africa
it settles on the first frame: Gambia inside Senegal

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Gambia or Lesotho: which border is stranger? And if a friend ever asks you,

disclaimer: Maps simplified. Borders as recognised by the country each video is about.
